title: Navigating Finances as a New UK NRI: Banking & Investments
description: Your residency status change to a UK Non-Resident Indian (NRI) significantly alters your financial obligations in both countries. It is mandatory to convert y.

faq.q: What is the definition of an NRI for tax purposes?
faq.a: An individual is generally considered an NRI if they have not resided in India for 182 days or more during the financial year, or if they have not resided in India for 365 days or more in the preceding four years and 120 days or more in the current financial year.

faq.q: Can I continue investing in my Indian mutual funds as a UK NRI?
faq.a: Yes, you can continue to hold existing mutual fund units. For new investments, you typically need to invest through an NRE or NRO account. Some fund houses may have specific restrictions based on your country of residence.

faq.q: What are the tax benefits of ISAs in the UK?
faq.a: ISAs offer tax-free growth on interest, capital gains, and dividends within the UK. Contributions are made from post-tax income, but withdrawals are also tax-free.

faq.q: How do I repatriate funds from my NRO account?
faq.a: You can repatriate funds from your NRO account up to USD 1 million per financial year, subject to tax clearance and necessary documentation from your bank. Funds from NRE accounts are freely repatriable.

faq.q: Should I close my PPF account after becoming an NRI?
faq.a: No, you are not required to close your PPF account. You can continue to hold it until maturity, but you cannot make new contributions to it once you become an NRI. The account will continue to earn tax-free interest.

faq.q: What happens to my Indian EPF account?
faq.a: Your Employees' Provident Fund (EPF) account can either be withdrawn (subject to certain conditions and tax implications) or kept active. You cannot make new contributions to it once you become an NRI. You can transfer it to an NPS account in some cases.
